items.title_en: Latent Reasoning in Continuous Space for Unified Multimodal Models
items.title_zh: 统一多模态模型在连续空间中的隐式推理（LARC）
items.abstract_en: Unified Multimodal Models (UMMs) achieve remarkable success on diverse multimodal understanding and generation tasks, yet they still struggle to effectively leverage language-based chain-of-thought reasoning for image generation. As a result, existing reasoning-augmented UMMs often fail to inherit the test-time scaling and fine-grained controllability observed in large language models. We attribute this failure to a fundamental modality mismatch: reasoning is performed in a discrete token space, whereas image generation operates in a continuous space. To bridge this gap, we introduce a Latent Reasoning framework in Continuous space (LARC), which alleviates the token-level bottleneck by reasoning over continuous hidden states. Specifically, the training framework consists of two stages: (i) curriculum supervised fine-tuning (SFT), and (ii) information-gain reinforcement learning (RL). First, the curriculum SFT stage gradually converts token-level reasoning into latent reasoning. Subsequently, the information-gain RL stage self-evolves latent reasoning without ground truth supervision. Experiments across diverse text-to-image generation benchmarks show that LARC consistently improves generation quality, prompt following, and compositional fidelity. Notably, LARC achieves state-of-the-art performance on GenEval with a 7%p gain over BAGEL and demonstrates clear test-time scaling behavior, outperforming token-based generation under both parallel and sequential test-time scaling strategies.
items.abstract_zh: 统一多模态模型（UMMs）在多模态理解与生成任务上表现优异，却难以有效利用基于语言的思维链推理来生成图像，因而无法继承大语言模型中观察到的测试时扩展与细粒度可控性。作者将这一失败归因于模态错配：推理发生在离散 token 空间，而图像生成在连续空间中进行。为此提出连续空间隐式推理框架 LARC，在连续隐状态上推理以缓解 token 级瓶颈。训练分两阶段：课程式监督微调（SFT）逐步将 token 级推理转化为隐式推理；随后信息增益强化学习在无真值监督下让隐式推理自演化。多组文生图基准显示，LARC 稳定提升生成质量、提示跟随与组合保真度，在 GenEval 上较 BAGEL 提升 7 个百分点，并展现明显的测试时扩展行为。
items.highlight_zh: 把推理搬进连续隐空间，破解模态错配
items.digest_zh:
研究问题：统一多模态模型（UMM）既能理解也能生成图像，但把大语言模型“先写推理链再出图”的做法搬过来效果不佳，既难像 LLM 那样靠增加测试时算力持续变好，也难以精细控制画面。
方法：作者指出根因是模态错配——文本推理发生在离散 token 上，图像生成却发生在连续特征空间，token 成了瓶颈。于是提出 LARC：直接在连续隐状态上做推理。训练分两步，先用课程式监督微调（SFT），把原本 token 级的推理逐步迁移为隐式推理；再用“信息增益”强化学习，在没有标准答案的情况下让隐式推理自我进化。
结果：在多组文本到图像基准上，生成质量、提示词跟随和组合关系准确性均稳定提升；GenEval 上比 BAGEL 高 7 个百分点，达到当时最优，并表现出清晰的测试时扩展——无论并行还是串行地增加推理算力都能继续涨点，且优于基于 token 的生成方式。
为何重要：它说明推理未必要写成文字，只有把推理对齐到生成所在的连续空间，多模态模型才能真正继承大语言模型的推理扩展红利，为可控、可扩展的图像生成提供新范式。
items.comment: Published as conference proceeding for NeurIPS 2026. Last two authors advised equally

rm.usage: 面向文生图生成的连续空间隐式推理，与自瞄、导航、决策等感知控制环节几乎无交集，最多只能做赛况示意图或宣传素材的生成，关联很弱。

items.title_en: HiFOR: Hierarchical Foresight with Action-Guided World Grounding for Vision-Language-Action Model
items.title_zh: HiFOR：面向视觉-语言-动作模型的动作引导世界接地分层前瞻
items.abstract_en: Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models have demonstrated promising capabilities in robotic manipulation by integrating visual perception, language understanding, and action generation. Recent advances have further incorporated future prediction to enhance the understanding of environmental dynamics and task progression. However, existing methods often model short-term dynamics and long-term task objectives separately, while directly incorporating predicted futures into action policies without sufficiently considering their relevance to current action requirements. To address these limitations, we propose HiFOR, a hierarchical foresight framework with action-guided world retrieval. Specifically, Hierarchical Foresight Prediction jointly predicts short-term state evolution, semantic milestones, and final goal states through a Hierarchical Dependency Mask (HDM), establishing dependencies across temporal horizons. Building upon these predictions, Structure-Aware Latent World Modeling organizes future latent representations along the horizon, view, and spatial dimensions to facilitate fine-grained retrieval. Furthermore, Action-Guided Factorized World Retrieval adaptively retrieves relevant future information from the structured latent world based on evolving action representations during denoising, providing targeted guidance for action generation. Extensive experiments on two simulation benchmarks and six real-world robotic manipulation tasks demonstrate the effectiveness of our approach.
items.abstract_zh: 视觉-语言-动作（VLA）模型融合视觉感知、语言理解与动作生成，在机器人操作中展现出潜力，近期工作还引入未来预测以增强对动态环境与任务进程的理解。但现有方法常将短期动态与长期目标分开建模，并把预测的未来直接注入动作策略，未充分考虑其与当前动作需求的相关性。为此提出 HiFOR：分层前瞻预测借助分层依赖掩码（HDM）联合预测短期状态演化、语义里程碑与最终目标状态；结构感知潜世界建模沿时间、视角、空间维度组织未来潜表示以支持细粒度检索；动作引导的因子化世界检索在去噪过程中依据演化的动作表示自适应检索相关未来信息。在两个仿真基准与六项真实机器人操作任务上验证了有效性。
items.highlight_zh: 分层预见未来，并按当前动作需求检索
items.digest_zh:
研究问题：VLA 模型做机器人操作时，引入“预测未来”有助于理解环境变化与任务进度，但现有做法往往把短期动态和长期目标分开建模，而且把预测出的未来直接喂给动作策略，没有判断这些未来信息与当前动作是否真的相关，容易引入干扰。
方法：提出 HiFOR 分层前瞻框架，包含三个部件。①分层前瞻预测：用分层依赖掩码（HDM）同时预测短期状态演化、语义里程碑和最终目标状态，在多个时间尺度之间建立依赖。②结构感知潜世界建模：把未来潜表示按时间、视角、空间三个维度组织成结构化的“潜世界”。③动作引导的因子化世界检索：在动作去噪过程中，根据不断演化的动作表示，从潜世界中自适应检索最相关的未来信息。
结果：在两个仿真基准和六项真实机器人操作任务上验证了方法的有效性，说明其能迁移到真实硬件。
为何重要：它把“预见未来”从粗放地灌给策略，变成按需检索、与当前动作对齐的引导信号，从而在长程操作中做出更靠谱的决策，提升了 VLA 在真实场景中的实用性。

rm.usage: 其分层前瞻+潜世界建模（预测短期状态与语义里程碑）可借鉴到重装机器人装配任务：预测能量单元/视觉标签的位姿演化并据此规划机械臂抓取与对接动作；不过面向桌面操作 VLA，需大量改造，属思路参考。

items.title_en: Venus-DefakerOne2: A Vision-Forensics Foundation Model with Broader Coverage
items.title_zh: Venus-DefakerOne2：覆盖范围更广的视觉取证基础模型
items.abstract_en: Real-world forgery is inherently heterogeneous: it manifests not only as digital manipulation but also as physical spoofing, and is carried not only by images but also by videos. Despite substantial progress, a unified anti-forgery foundation model covering such a broad threat spectrum remains absent. In this paper, we present Venus-DefakerOne2, which substantially extends the forensic capability boundary along both the forgery-form and media-type dimensions. Trained on tens of millions of open-source and in-house samples, it incorporates two key designs. Tide-Style-Tuning alternates LoRA and full-parameter fine-tuning to balance computational efficiency, generalization, and hard-sample fitting while mitigating catastrophic forgetting. Entropy-based Test Adaptation determines the optimal prediction modality by analyzing prediction entropy. Venus-DefakerOne2 achieves new state-of-the-art performance across a comprehensive suite of benchmarks, including DeepFake faces (96.7%), AI-generated images (93.3%), tampered documents (87.6%), manipulated natural images (89.6%), physical spoofs (93.1%), and AI-generated videos (96.0%). It significantly outperforms both specialized expert models and its predecessor, DefakerOne, establishing itself as a powerful and versatile foundation model for binary-decision forensic tasks.
items.abstract_zh: 现实中的伪造具有异构性：既有数字篡改，也有物理欺骗；载体既有图像，也有视频。尽管已有诸多进展，覆盖如此宽威胁谱的统一反伪造基础模型仍然缺失。本文提出 Venus-DefakerOne2，沿伪造形态与媒体类型两个维度大幅扩展取证能力边界。模型在数千万开源与自研样本上训练，含两项关键设计：Tide-Style-Tuning 交替进行 LoRA 与全参数微调，在计算效率、泛化性与难样本拟合之间取得平衡，并缓解灾难性遗忘；基于熵的测试自适应通过分析预测熵确定最优预测模态。该模型在整套基准上刷新最优，包括 DeepFake 人脸 96.7%、AI 生成图像 93.3%、被篡改文档 87.6%、被操纵自然图像 89.6%、物理欺骗 93.1% 与 AI 生成视频 96.0%，显著超越专用专家模型与前代 DefakerOne。
items.highlight_zh: 一个基础模型统一图像、视频与物理欺骗取证
items.digest_zh:
研究问题：现实中的伪造并不单一——既有像素级的数字篡改，也有翻拍、假体等物理欺骗；既有图片，也有视频。现有反伪造模型多只针对某一类伪造或某一种媒介，缺少能覆盖如此宽威胁谱的统一基础模型。
方法：作者提出 Venus-DefakerOne2，同时在“伪造形态”和“媒体类型”两个方向扩展取证边界，用数千万量级的开源加自研样本训练。两项关键设计：一是 Tide-Style-Tuning，交替使用 LoRA 微调与全参数微调，在算力效率、泛化能力和难样本拟合之间求平衡，并缓解灾难性遗忘；二是基于熵的测试时自适应，通过分析预测熵自动选择最优的预测分支。
结果：在一整套基准上刷新最优——DeepFake 人脸 96.7%、AI 生成图像 93.3%、被篡改文档 87.6%、被操纵自然图像 89.6%、物理欺骗 93.1%、AI 生成视频 96.0%，明显超过各领域的专用专家模型以及上一代 DefakerOne。
为何重要：它把真假二分类的取证任务统一进一个基础模型，覆盖图像、视频与物理欺骗，为内容安全审核提供单一、可扩展、易部署的底座，而不必为每种伪造各训练一个专用检测器。

rm.usage: 伪造检测/取证模型与赛场任务基本无关，RM 中不存在需要鉴别篡改图像或视频的环节，可用于赛后录像素材审核这类边缘场景，实用度很低。

items.title_en: CaPtain: A Pipeline for Post-Training Code-as-Policy Robot Agents
items.title_zh: CaPtain：面向代码即策略机器人智能体的后训练流水线
items.abstract_en: Across coding, web, and tool-use tasks, language-model agents are now routinely trained with the same recipe: supervised fine-tuning (SFT) to learn the interface, then multi-turn reinforcement learning (RL) to master it. Code-as-policy (CaP) casts robot manipulation in the same form, as the policy writes code against robot APIs and reads back the results, so the same recipe should apply. Yet existing CaP agents sidestep training: they either prompt closed frontier models or delegate manipulation to pre-trained vision-language-action models (VLAs) and high-level skills, while small open vision-language models (VLMs) fail outright. We present CaPtain, an open post-training pipeline that turns a small open VLM into a capable CaP agent, with no VLA, frontier model, or privileged state at test time. CaPtain trains and deploys the policy inside CaPtain-Harness, which exposes low-level perception, geometry, and guarded-motion primitives across simulation and real hardware. We first align the base model via SFT on synthetic trajectories generated with GPT-6 Astra, then apply multi-turn RL. Multi-turn RL must credit tens of agent requests, whose physical effects often surface turns later, from a single end-of-episode outcome. We therefore introduce a physical critic that reads privileged simulator state, never seen by the policy, and credits each request by how much it changes the predicted chance of success. Starting from Qwen3.5-4B (0% zero-shot), CaPtain-4B reaches 55.4% held-out LIBERO success after SFT and 73.8% after RL. On LIBERO-PRO, it reaches 78.5%, surpassing several frontier-model agents, and its RL gains persist across three perturbation suites (+17.6 to +21.2 points). Without target-domain training, it attains 83.3% on SimplerEnv WidowX, exceeds frontier models on CaP-Bench, and runs on a real robot after simulation-only adaptation. We release all code, data, and model weights.
items.abstract_zh: 在编程、网页与工具调用任务中，语言模型智能体普遍采用同一套配方：先用监督微调（SFT）学会接口，再用多轮强化学习（RL）掌握它。代码即策略（CaP）把机器人操作建模为编写针对机器人 API 的代码并读取返回结果，理应同样适用，但现有 CaP 智能体都绕开了训练：或提示闭源前沿模型，或把操作委托给预训练 VLA 与高层技能，而小型开源视觉语言模型则直接失败。本文提出 CaPtain，一条开放后训练流水线，可将小型开源 VLM 训练为能干的 CaP 智能体，测试时不依赖 VLA、前沿模型或特权状态。策略在 CaPtain-Harness 中训练部署；先用合成轨迹做 SFT 对齐，再做多轮 RL，并引入读取特权仿真状态的“物理评论家”，按每次请求对预测成功概率的改变量分配信用。
items.highlight_zh: 小开源 VLM 靠后训练成为可用机器人代码策略
items.digest_zh:
研究问题：语言模型智能体在写代码、网页操作、调用工具上通常走“先 SFT 学接口、再多轮 RL 练熟”的路线。代码即策略（CaP）把机器人操作也写成对机器人 API 的代码，按理同样适用，可现有 CaP 智能体都跳过了训练：要么直接提示闭源前沿模型，要么把操作交给预训练 VLA 和高层技能，小型开源视觉语言模型则完全做不动。
方法：作者提出 CaPtain，一条开放的后训练流水线，把小型开源 VLM 变成能干的 CaP 智能体，测试时不需要 VLA、前沿模型或特权状态。策略在 CaPtain-Harness 中训练和部署，该环境在仿真与真机上提供底层感知、几何计算和带保护的移动原语。先用在仿真中由大模型生成的合成轨迹做 SFT 对齐，再做多轮 RL。难点是一次回合结束时才有一个成败信号，却要归因到几十次智能体请求上，而物理效果常常延迟数轮才显现。为此引入“物理评论家”，它读取策略永远看不到的特权仿真状态，按每次请求对预测成功概率的改变量来分配信用。
结果：从 Qwen3.5-4B（零样本 0%）出发，SFT 后在留出 LIBERO 上达 55.4%，RL 后达 73.8%；LIBERO-PRO 上 78.5%，超过若干前沿模型智能体；RL 收益在三套扰动下保持（+17.6 至 +21.2 点）；未做目标域训练时，SimplerEnv WidowX 上达 83.3%。
为何重要：它证明小模型配上合适的后训练与信用分配，也能成为实用的机器人代码策略，摆脱对闭源大模型和专用 VLA 的依赖。

rm.usage: 代码即策略智能体的后训练流程，可参考用于工程机器人高层任务脚本的自动化生成与调试（如装配流程代码），但 RM 底层为强实时嵌入式 C++，难以直接落地。

items.title_en: Training Foundation Models with a Single Algorithm
items.title_zh: 用单一算法训练基础模型
items.abstract_en: Foundation models are typically trained in stages: pretraining, midtraining, supervised fine-tuning (SFT), and reinforcement learning (RL), with changes in both data and learning algorithms. We show that this algorithmic separation is not fundamental. By deriving suitable RL objectives as maximum-likelihood fitting to model-generated target distributions, we place all of these stages under a single likelihood-based training algorithm, unified training. This perspective turns the foundation-model training lifecycle into a problem of choosing which data to train on, in what proportions, and when, with conventional staged training as a special case. We instantiate this framework in a unified training system that mixes static data and RL generations within a single trainer. Across controlled and real-world experiments, unified training improves the accuracy-compute tradeoff and task coverage while preserving broader capabilities, and provides a stronger starting point for continual learning. This work lays the groundwork for a unified science of foundation-model training, connecting mathematical principles, training infrastructure, and the development of model capabilities.
items.abstract_zh: 基础模型通常分阶段训练：预训练、中训、监督微调（SFT）和强化学习（RL），且各阶段的数据与学习算法都会变化。我们表明这种算法层面的割裂并非本质。通过把合适的 RL 目标推导为对模型自生成目标分布的最大似然拟合，我们将上述所有阶段纳入同一个基于似然的训练算法——统一训练。这一视角把基础模型的训练生命周期转化为一个选择问题：在什么数据上训练、以何种比例、在何时训练；传统分阶段训练只是其特例。我们以统一训练系统实例化该框架，在单一训练器中混合静态数据与 RL 生成。在受控与真实实验中，统一训练改善了准确率—算力权衡与任务覆盖，同时保留更广泛的能力，并为持续学习提供更强的起点。该工作为基础模型训练的统一科学奠定基础，连接数学原理、训练基础设施与模型能力的发展。
items.highlight_zh: 用最大似然统一预训练到 RL，把分阶段训练变成选数据的问题
items.digest_zh:
1. 研究了什么问题：今天的基础模型要分好几步训练——先大规模预训练，再中训，再做监督微调（SFT），最后做强化学习（RL）。每一步不仅换数据，还换算法，整个流程像几条流水线拼起来，难以统一理解与优化。作者追问：这种算法上的分家是必须的吗？

2. 用了什么方法：作者做了一个理论上的“归并”。他们证明，只要把合适的强化学习目标重新推导成“对模型自己生成的目标分布做最大似然拟合”，那么预训练、中训、SFT、RL 其实都可以写成同一个基于似然的训练算法，称为统一训练（unified training）。在这个视角下，分阶段训练只是特例；真正要决策的只有三件事：在哪些数据上训练、以什么比例混合、什么时候训练。作者还搭建了一个统一训练系统，在同一个训练器里同时喂静态数据和 RL 生成的数据。

3. 有什么结果：在受控实验和真实实验中，统一训练在准确率与算力的权衡上更好，覆盖的任务更多，同时没有牺牲模型的其他广泛能力；而且它训练出的模型作为持续学习的起点更强。

4. 为何重要：这篇工作把原本靠经验拼接的训练流程，提升为可以用同一套数学语言讨论的问题，把数学原理、训练基础设施和能力演化串在一条线上，为“基础模型训练的统一科学”开了个头。对工程团队而言，这意味着未来可能不再需要维护多套算法管线，而是集中精力设计数据配比与调度策略。

rm.usage: 统一训练框架把预训练/SFT/RL 合成单一似然目标，可作为战队自瞄、决策等强化学习训练流水线的工程参考，用于简化 sim 中多阶段训练与持续学习，但不是可直接搬用的算法。

items.title_en: WorldBridge: Bridging Video and Action for Task Generalization in World Action Models
items.title_zh: WorldBridge：在世界动作模型中桥接视频与动作以实现任务泛化
items.abstract_en: Achieving the broad task generalization of embodied models in physical environments remains a central challenge in robot learning. We study this challenge in World Action Models (WAMs) through two complementary capabilities: video generalization, which predicts the visual evolution of new tasks, and action generalization, which translates these predictions into executable behavior through a video-to-action bridge. By varying video and action supervision for tasks outside an initial training set, we examine their respective contributions to task transfer. On RoboTwin 2.0, using only in-distribution video-action supervision yields a 25.07% success rate on out-of-distribution tasks. Introducing videos of these tasks without their action labels raises success to 55.90%, while adding just one action-labeled demonstration per task further improves it to 70.70%. These findings suggest that broader video coverage enables task transfer by leveraging existing inverse-dynamics capabilities, while even sparse action supervision further strengthens those capabilities. Guided by this perspective, we introduce WorldBridge, a WAM with separate video and action experts connected through structured attention and trained with joint flow matching. WorldBridge incorporates visual memory at two temporal scales and action forcing, alongside a unified data processing pipeline that standardizes and filters heterogeneous robot trajectories and egocentric hand-derived supervision. Across multiple manipulation benchmarks, WorldBridge achieves state-of-the-art performance among the compared methods, including 96.23% on RoboTwin 2.0 full data setting and 80.9% on clean to random setting, 82.8% on RoboCasa GR1 TableTop, and 57.6% on DOMINO Level-1. Our study highlights the complementary roles of video prediction and action grounding in developing robots that generalize across tasks.
items.abstract_zh: 让具身模型在物理环境中实现广泛的任务泛化，仍是机器人学习的核心难题。我们在世界动作模型（WAMs）中通过两种互补能力研究该问题：视频泛化——预测新任务的视觉演化；动作泛化——通过视频到动作的桥接把预测转化为可执行行为。通过在初始训练集之外的任务上改变视频与动作监督，我们考察二者各自对任务迁移的贡献。在 RoboTwin 2.0 上，仅使用分布内的视频—动作监督得到 25.07% 的成功率；引入这些任务的无动作标签视频后提升至 55.90%；每个任务再加一个带动作标签的示范后进一步提升至 70.70%。这表明更广的视频覆盖能借助已有的逆动力学能力实现任务迁移，而即使稀疏的动作监督也能进一步增强该能力。据此我们提出 WorldBridge，其视频专家与动作专家分离，通过结构化注意力连接并以联合 flow matching 训练，融合两个时间尺度的视觉记忆与动作强制（action forcing），并配有统一数据处理管线，用于标准化和过滤异构机器人轨迹与第一人称手部数据。在多个操作基准上，WorldBridge 在对比方法中取得最优性能，包括 RoboTwin 2.0 全数据设置的 96.23%、clean to random 设置的 80.9%、RoboCasa GR1 TableTop 的 82.8% 以及 DOMINO Level-1 的 57.6%。
items.highlight_zh: 无动作标签视频即可大幅提升新任务成功率，WorldBridge 刷新多项基准
items.digest_zh:
1. 研究了什么问题：机器人想在新环境、新任务里干活，泛化是最大门槛。论文在世界动作模型（WAMs）框架下把泛化拆成两半：一是“视频泛化”，即模型能否想象出新任务场景会怎样演变；二是“动作泛化”，即能否把想象中的画面转成真正可执行的动作。作者想知道这两部分各自的监督信号对迁移到底贡献多大。

2. 用了什么方法：先做诊断实验——在初始训练集之外的任务上，分别改变视频数据和动作标签的供给量，看成功率怎么变。在 RoboTwin 2.0 上：只用分布内的视频—动作监督时为 25.07%；把这些新任务的视频给模型看但不给动作标签，成功率升到 55.90%；每个任务再补一条带动作标签的示范，进一步到 70.70%。结论是：更广的视频覆盖能借助模型已有的逆动力学能力完成迁移，而哪怕很稀疏的动作监督也能显著加强这一能力。基于此提出 WorldBridge：视频专家与动作专家分开，用结构化注意力连接，以联合 flow matching 训练；还引入两个时间尺度的视觉记忆和 action forcing，并配套一套统一的数据处理管线，标准化并过滤异构机器人轨迹与第一人称手部数据。

3. 有什么结果：在多个人形/机械臂操作基准上取得对比方法中的最好成绩：RoboTwin 2.0 全数据 96.23%，clean to random 80.9%，RoboCasa GR1 TableTop 82.8%，DOMINO Level-1 57.6%。

4. 为何重要：它给出了一个很实用的数据配比直觉——多收视频、少收动作标签也能换来泛化，这对数据昂贵、标注困难的机器人领域意义很大，也为“视频预测 + 动作桥接”这一路线提供了清晰的结构设计与工程范式。

rm.usage: 世界动作模型用大量无动作标签视频提升任务泛化，可借鉴到仿真环境中用比赛录像增强操作/装配策略训练，但 RoboTwin 类操作基准与 RM 任务形态（自瞄、导航、对抗）差距大，关联有限。

items.title_en: OpenFlyV2: An onboard vision-language-action model for aerial perception and navigation
items.title_zh: OpenFlyV2：面向空中感知与导航的机载视觉-语言-动作模型
items.abstract_en: Human cognition flexibly draws on a shared perceptual foundation to understand environments, attend to referenced entities, reason about spatial relationships, and act. Endowing aerial robots with an analogous functional organization remains challenging, as existing systems are often specialized for individual capabilities, dependent on offboard computation, or unable to sustain closed-loop operation on resource-constrained platforms. We present OpenFlyV2, a unified onboard vision-language-action architecture that uses a shared vision-language representation to support semantic understanding, language-grounded perception, spatial reasoning, and continuous aerial control within a single model. A compact action expert converts the shared multimodal context into short-horizon flight waypoints, while motion-aware temporal memory and action priors reduce the computational cost of closed-loop execution. We construct \dataset{}, a simulation-based dataset comprising approximately 70,000 navigation trajectories and 60,000 vision-language instruction--response pairs. OpenFlyV2 generates action chunks, each comprising 12 waypoints, entirely onboard at 10 Hz using an NVIDIA Jetson Orin NX. It transfers zero-shot from simulation to physical quadrotor flight, achieving a 48\% navigation success rate across four real-world environments without real-world aerial training data. Extensive results demonstrate that broad vision-language competence and continuous closed-loop flight can coexist within a single model on a resource-constrained aerial platform. Code will be made publicly available at https://github.com/Ideal-ljl/AeroBrain.

rm.usage: 机载统一 VLA 架构在算力受限平台上做语义理解、空间关系推理与动作闭环，可参考其结构设计哨兵机器人的高层语义决策（如按区域语义选择巡逻/防守动作）并与底层导航解耦；无人机场景需改造成地面哨兵方案。
rm.task: 哨兵机器人自主导航与决策

items.title_en: RoboArchitect: Automating the Design of Robotic Agents with Persistent Memory
items.title_zh: RoboArchitect：自动化设计具有持久记忆的机器人智能体
items.abstract_en: Recent work shows that a frozen robot policy performs far better inside an agent harness, where control code decides when to query the policy, consult vision tools, or command the arm directly. Yet today these harnesses are built by hand and redesigned for each new robot or benchmark. We show that harness design can be automated, offering a strong alternative to finetuning on a novel setup. In RoboArchitect, a coding model observes a robot's rollouts, diagnoses failures, and iteratively revises the harness around the frozen policy. The harness evolves on a set of episodes for its optimization and is evaluated on held-out scenes and tasks. Without updating any model weights, RoboArchitect raises average success from 9.7% to 43.3% on unseen scenes (4.5x) and from 12.7% to 40.2% on unseen tasks (3.2x), across multiple benchmarks and policies. The gains are largest where the benchmark is far from the policy's training data: wrapping a general-purpose policy, the evolved harness yields a specialist that often outperforms even the finetuned version. Intuitive control strategies are automatically designed, such as lifting a jammed arm clear or reaching in horizontally when an obstacle blocks the way from above. The harness also evolves its own persistent memory, carrying learned experience, such as effective grasp depths, into later decisions. These results suggest that substantial headroom in robotic manipulation lies in the agent harness, and its design can be effectively automated and optimized without weight updates.

rm.usage: 自动搜索智能体 harness 的思路可用于搭建工程机器人/哨兵的“冻结策略+调度代码”框架并自动迭代，但需要大量仿真回放和失败诊断基建，短期内难以用于赛场，关联较弱。

items.title_en: Learning Quality-Controllable Robot Policies with Iterative Hindsight Relabeling
items.title_zh: 基于迭代事后重标记学习质量可控的机器人策略
items.abstract_en: Robot policy evaluation often relies on a binary success signal for task completion. In real-world deployment, however, desired execution behaviors are also defined by quality attributes such as execution speed and motion smoothness, which need to be dynamically controlled according to task requirements. To address this, we introduce Quality-Controllable Policy (QCP), a robot policy that enables inference-time control over both individual quality attributes and their combinations. To extend the controllable quality range beyond initial demonstrations, we further propose an iterative hindsight relabeling loop: QCP collects online rollouts under target quality labels, adds successful trajectories to the dataset, relabels the accumulated trajectories in hindsight according to their measured quality, and fine-tunes the policy. Experiments on Robomimic and RoboEval demonstrate that QCP consistently improves both task execution quality and success rates across iterations, producing successful rollouts that exceed the quality of the initial demonstrations. Finally, we validate QCP on real-world manipulation tasks, where controlling speed increases throughput in conveyor operations and controlling transport stability improves success when carrying wine glasses, demonstrating that quality-controllable policies yield practical gains in physical deployment.

rm.usage: QCP 可在仿真中训练哨兵导航或战术决策策略时，按任务需求调节动作速度与平滑度；需把质量属性改造成 RM 可度量的指标。

items.title_en: WorkIng: A Real-World and Synthetic Highway Work-Zone Benchmark Dataset for Autonomous Navigation
items.title_zh: WorkIng：面向自主导航的真实世界与合成高速公路工作区基准数据集
items.abstract_en: Highway work zones are critical edge cases for autonomous vehicles (AVs), combining atypical geometries and jurisdiction-specific regulations that existing benchmarks fail to capture: real-world datasets lack 360° multi-modal, full-scene 3D work zone annotation, and no single recorded site can span the layouts and regulatory variants needed for generalizable models. We present WorkIng, a dual-domain benchmark and training resource. WorkIng-Highway provides a 360° multi-modal work zone benchmark with synchronized 128-channel LiDAR, six RGB cameras, and RTK-GPS across 32 km, yielding 12,000+ annotated frames and 227,399 tracked 3D bounding boxes. WorkIng-CARLA complements this with procedural simulation spanning 24 regulation-aware scenarios across six canonical topologies and six international traffic standards, populated by 100+ custom 3D assets. Benchmarking representative 3D detection and end-to-end planning architectures shows that real-world data remains the primary performance driver, and that scenario-stratified synthetic augmentation improves architectures across 2D recognition, 3D detection, and trajectory planning. Resources: https://github.com/cvims/WorkIng
items.comment: Accepted to WACV 2027. 19 pages including supplementary material. (c) 2027 IEEE. Personal use of this material is permitted

rm.usage: 高速公路施工区多模态数据集与 RM 室内战场差异很大，只能借鉴其 360° 多模态标注和边缘场景基准构建思路，不能直接用于哨兵导航。
rm.task: 哨兵机器人自主导航与决策

items.title_en: GRIT: Gradient Masking for Visually Misgrounded Tokens in Text-Rich Reasoning
items.title_zh: GRIT：面向文本丰富推理中视觉错误关联词元的梯度掩蔽
items.abstract_en: Reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards (RLVR) has recently been extended to vision-language models (VLMs), yet its effectiveness remains limited for text-rich reasoning tasks. We highlight a key factor contributing to this limitation: models frequently arrive at correct final answers despite misperceiving visual information during intermediate steps. We define this phenomenon as Correct-but-Visually-Misgrounded Reasoning (CVMR). Because standard RLVR rewards only final-answer correctness, it fails to differentiate between properly grounded and misgrounded reasoning, reinforcing both equally. Through token-level analysis, we reveal that CVMR tokens exhibit distinct attention patterns that differ systematically from well-grounded ones. Based on this observation, we propose GRIT, a training framework that incorporates visual grounding into RLVR to mitigate the impact of CVMR. Furthermore, to address the lack of text-rich reasoning benchmarks that allow for systematic evaluation across text length and reasoning depth, we introduce GRIT-Bench. Experiments demonstrate that GRIT significantly improves both reasoning accuracy and grounding fidelity over existing RLVR methods.

rm.usage: 该工作针对文本丰富 VLM 的视觉错误关联，与装甲板识别、能量机关等 RM 视觉任务关联很弱，基本用不上。

items.title_en: RoSAMDepth: Robust Self-supervised Depth Estimation Leveraging Segment Anything Model
items.title_zh: RoSAMDepth：利用Segment Anything Model的鲁棒自监督深度估计
items.abstract_en: Robust depth estimation aims to maintain high-quality depths across diverse conditions. However, most existing methods estimate depth without taking into account the object-level information. As a result, the predicted depth may easily deviate within objects and become blurred under adverse conditions. To overcome this weakness, we propose RoSAMDepth, a novel framework that can assist robust self-supervised depth estimation in leveraging rich and diverse object-level priors from the Segment Anything Model (SAM). We focus on incorporating object-level information across three key aspects: a segment-guided representation contrasting method that injects object-level awareness into the feature representation space; an adaptive regional outlier masking strategy combined with a regional Gaussian likelihood loss that enforces regional depth smoothness; and an object-level reliability estimation strategy that mitigates the influence of unreliable supervision. Extensive experiments across multiple datasets and diverse weather conditions demonstrate that our method produces sharper, more accurate depth predictions, consistently outperforming state-of-the-art methods. Our code is available at https://github.com/xagao/RoSAMDepth.
items.comment: 13 pages, 8 figures, including supplementary material. Published in CVPR 2026

rm.usage: RoSAMDepth 可用 SAM 物体级先验提升复杂光照下深度估计，适合作为哨兵或工程机器人单目避障与距离感知的候选，但需嵌入式适配。
rm.task: 哨兵机器人自主导航与决策

items.title_en: Decoding Geometry, Not Tokens: Efficient VLMs for Robot Affordance and Trajectory Prediction
items.title_zh: 解码几何而非词元：面向机器人可供性与轨迹预测的高效VLM
items.abstract_en: Predicting where to grasp and how to move is fundamentally a geometry problem. Vision-language models treat it as language generation instead. They tokenize spatial coordinates into text and decode them autoregressively. This mechanism ignores spatial structure and truncates continuous precision. Errors compound across coordinate tokens during decoding. In this paper, we show that compact off-the-shelf VLMs with 0.5-2B parameters already encode rich spatial information in their intermediate hidden states. Autoregressive decoding is the dominant bottleneck for trajectory prediction, while affordance prediction depends additionally on feature depth and decoder architecture. We expose the latent spatial information with a lightweight, geometry-compatible prediction head that attaches to a frozen backbone. It reads features from an intermediate hidden layer, conditions a learned query on the task instruction and refines it via cross-attention over the visual tokens to regress affordance boxes and trajectory waypoints directly as continuous values, without modifying the backbone. We evaluate on ShareRobot-Bench and AGD20K. Our 2B variant reduces trajectory error by over 60% and improves ShareRobot-Bench affordance mAP by 85% relative to the autoregressive baseline. It approaches RoboBrain on trajectory prediction (0.251 vs 0.191 DFD) at 3.8x higher throughput. These results demonstrate a favorable accuracy-efficiency trade-off for instruction-conditioned 2D geometric prediction.
items.comment: IEEE/CVF Winter Conference on Applications of Computer Vision (WACV 2027)

rm.usage: 可把紧凑 VLM 的几何可供性与轨迹预测思路用于工程机器人视觉装配，辅助抓取位姿和机械臂运动预测；需针对 RM 标签与装配任务微调。

items.title_en: CausalXRL: Explainable Reinforcement Learning through Causal Graph Reasoning
items.title_zh: CausalXRL：通过因果图推理实现可解释强化学习
items.abstract_en: Reinforcement learning is a powerful paradigm for training autonomous agents and has achieved impressive performance in complex environments. However, this success often comes at the cost of interpretability, diminishing trust and complicating efforts to debug and improve agent behavior. To address these challenges, we introduce CausalXRL, a novel framework for explainable reinforcement learning (XRL). A key feature of CausalXRL is its use of causal graph reasoning, which provides transparent, structured, multi-level explanations of agent decision-making. We validate CausalXRL through comprehensive case studies and a two-part evaluation: (1) a quantitative analysis of explanation fidelity and causal-structure learning efficiency in benchmark RL environments, and (2) a qualitative expert study assessing explainability in the real-time strategy (RTS) benchmark MicroRTS. The quantitative results show that CausalXRL can provide faithful explanations while efficiently learning causal structures, and the qualitative expert study suggests that participants found CausalXRL useful for inspecting high-level RTS strategies.
items.comment: Accepted to ICML 2026 - full paper - main track

rm.usage: CausalXRL 可用于事后解释和调试仿真中训练出的哨兵或多机战术策略，帮助定位决策异常，但因果图建模成本较高。

items.title_en: FOCUS: First-Order Control Using Optimal Transport Supervision for Imitation from Observations
items.title_zh: FOCUS：利用最优传输监督的一阶控制用于从观测中模仿学习
items.abstract_en: Imitation learning from observations must recover behavior from state-only demonstrations without known temporal correspondence. Differentiable simulators provide pathwise policy gradients, but differentiating through long, contact-rich trajectories can make optimization unstable. We introduce FOCUS, which combines local optimal-transport alignment with short-horizon differentiable actor-critic learning. FOCUS matches agent rollout windows to multiple sampled expert segments using a soft best-of-$K$ objective that emphasizes locally compatible matches. The resulting transport-based costs provide differentiable imitation rewards, while a learned critic bootstraps value beyond the rollout horizon. FOCUS requires neither temporally aligned trajectories nor expert-aligned initialization or teacher forcing. Across contact-rich locomotion tasks in DFlex, including a musculoskeletal humanoid controlled by 152 muscle activations, FOCUS improves sample efficiency and training stability over adversarial imitation-from-observation methods and prior differentiable imitation baselines.
items.comment: Accepted at the NeurIPS 2026 Workshop on Physical Understanding for Decision-Making

rm.usage: FOCUS 的从观测模仿学习可用于仿真中利用专家演示训练云台跟踪或哨兵导航策略，降低奖励设计难度；需搭建可微仿真与演示数据。

items.title_en: A Multi-Layer Navigation System for Smart Wheelchairs with a Limited Input Interface
items.title_zh: 面向输入接口受限的智能轮椅的多层导航系统
items.abstract_en: Smart wheelchairs are robotic devices that gather information from the surroundings and allow people to safely drive through various environments. They usually rely on the interpretation of high-level user's intentions, typically decoded through human-robot interface (HRI) or brain-machine interface (BMI). However, navigating in an unknown environment and accurately understanding user commands remain significant challenges. Misinterpretation of commands or the environment can lead to user frustration, distrust of the system, or even unsafe situations. In this paper, we present a novel Multi-Layer Navigation System (MLNS) for a smart wheelchair that enables navigation in unknown environments while interpreting and safely contextualizing user's intentions even in the case of limited and faulty commands. The stack relies on a Virtual Sensors-Driven Potential Fields (ViSPF) method for obstacle detection that accounts for the wheelchair's actual size, a Model Predictive Control (MPC) module for trajectory generation, and an open-vocabulary computer vision algorithm for target identification. Finally, a system based on Priority Queue (PQ) was implemented for target selection. We validated our system on a real smart wheelchair with experiments involving 10 participants without disabilities, including scenarios with faulty input interfaces. The results demonstrate the robustness and effectiveness of our system in real-world environments, proving its potential for practical applications in assistive technologies.
items.comment: 8 pages, 6 figures, 3 tables. Presented at IROS 2026 (IEEE/RSJ International Conference on Intelligent Robots and Systems); to appear in the conference proceedings

rm.usage: 多层导航架构可借鉴到哨兵在未知场地中的安全避障与分层决策，但其智能轮椅人机接口和意图解码部分不适用于全自动哨兵。
rm.task: 哨兵机器人自主导航与决策

items.title_en: MotorSense: A Video-EMG Dataset of Motoric Representations for Action Understanding
items.title_zh: MotorSense：用于动作理解的动作表征视频-EMG数据集
items.abstract_en: Computer vision models learn hand action only from its visual consequences, without access to the underlying embodied motor signals. We address this absence with MotorSense, the first large-scale paired egocentric video and surface electromyography (EMG) dataset. MotorSense pairs bimanual EMG bands with egocentric video and yields synchronized video, bimanual EMG and IMU, and audio across 100 hours of unscripted manipulation. EMG offers a powerful scalable alternative to manual annotation: it captures finger movement, hand configuration, and the forces exerted between hand and environment as a dense signal free of occlusion and labeler bias, whereas manual annotation is costly, subjective, and unreliable under occlusion. We use MotorSense to learn sensorimotor alignment, producing an organization of action that is shared across the visual and motoric spaces, through cross-modal pre-training between video and EMG. The resultant vision models are then transferred to downstream tasks that benefit from sensorimotor alignment: in this case, action recognition, 3D hand reconstruction, and 3D contact reconstruction. We further demonstrate a generative application in which EMG motor signals are used to condition a video diffusion model, yielding videos of fine-grained hand manipulation. Across four action-centric computer vision tasks and eight popular video datasets, we demonstrate that sensorimotor alignment provides a stronger foundation for visual representation learning than conventional self-supervised learning methods over video, outperforming every baseline across all tasks and datasets evaluated.
items.comment: NeurIPS 2026. 27 pages, 9 figures, 5 tables. Project page: https://www.cs.umd.edu/~edessale/motorsense/

rm.usage: 与RM关联很弱：第一视角视频+EMG的手部动作数据集不适用于轮式机器人自瞄/导航；最多为工程机器人视觉装配的人手操作理解提供思路，但传感器与任务不匹配。

items.title_en: Before We Adapt: The Zero-Shot Generalization Bottleneck in Continual World Models
items.title_zh: 适应之前：持续世界模型中的零样本泛化瓶颈
items.abstract_en: Continual reinforcement learning (CRL) requires agents to operate under environmental changes while reusing prior knowledge whenever possible. We argue that model-based reinforcement learning provides a promising framework for this setting because learned world models (WMs) can, in principle, support change detection, knowledge reuse, adaptation, and acquisition of new knowledge. However, such benefits depend heavily on whether the learned model can generalize beyond the contexts in which it was trained. In this work, we propose to formulate this problem with a contextual Markov decision process in which context is decomposed into behavioral and physical components. This view organizes continual WM learning into reuse, adaptation, and acquisition of new knowledge. As a first step, we study direct reuse when behavioral rules remain unchanged. Using Dyna-Q and TD-MPC in controlled FourRooms tasks, we find that zero-shot reuse can degrade substantially under physical-context changes and that this behavior depends strongly on the observation representation used by the WM. Additional ablation studies and latent-space diagnostics suggest that learned representations do not automatically provide the invariances needed for reuse. These results identify representation generalization as an important bottleneck for reliable world-model reuse in CRL.
items.comment: Accepted to Continual World Models workshop @ NeurIPS 2026

rm.usage: 可用于仿真环境中基于世界模型的持续强化学习训练，让哨兵或战术策略在场地/对手变化时检测变化并复用知识；需将C-MDP设定改造到RM仿真。

items.title_en: Steering Vectors as a Training Signal in LLM Post-Training
items.title_zh: 引导向量作为 LLM 后训练中的训练信号
items.abstract_en: Steering vectors (SVs) are residual-stream directions that shift the behavior of LLMs when added to hidden states at inference time. While prior work has mainly used SVs as post-hoc controls, we ask whether the same directions can also guide parameter updates during post-training. We study this question across supervised learning, including SFT and distillation, and reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards (RLVR). Our framework considers two intervention regimes: a hidden-state hook during teacher-forced supervised training, and an advantage-repair mechanism on wrong rollouts in GRPO. For each regime, we analyze three design axes, which are the steering direction, its placement, and the operation used to combine it with training. In supervised settings, SV injection improves over plain SFT and distillation, with gains scaling with the off-policy gap and reaching up to a $12\%$ improvement when distilling from thinking-mode teachers. These gains hold across three random seeds. In RL settings, applying a correctness-contrast direction as advantage repair on wrong rollouts, including otherwise zero-gradient all-wrong groups, recovers a learning signal that transfers to held-out math benchmarks and acts as a composable auxiliary signal that adds to existing zero-variance remedies such as entropy-aware advantage shaping. We further identify three failure boundaries. In detail, code generation can break the direction, cross-family layer transfer can break the placement, and inference-time application on an SV-trained checkpoint can break the intervention regime. Together, these results establish steering vectors as a conditional but effective training signal for LLM post-training. Our code is available here.

rm.usage: 与RM算法任务基本无关；LLM引导向量用于语言模型后训练，不能直接用于自瞄、导航或战术决策。

items.title_en: SketchDirector: Complex Scene Sketching via Agentic Layout Reasoning and Detail Refinement
items.title_zh: SketchDirector：通过智能体布局推理与细节精炼实现复杂场景素描
items.abstract_en: Existing sketch generation methods often rely on image guidance and are largely limited to individual objects or simplified scenes, leaving text-guided complex scene sketching underexplored. We present SketchDirector, an agentic framework that mimics the human sketching workflow for automatic multi-concept scene sketching. Given a scene-level text prompt, SketchDirector first employs a large language model~(LLM) to decompose the scene into multiple draft assets, where each is represented by a set of Bézier curves. Then, an agentic reasoning loop iteratively plans and executes their spatial arrangement, guided by self-evolving memory. Finally, a detail refinement module leverages diffusion priors to enhance sketch quality while preserving geometric structure. To support future research and applications in multi-concept scene sketch generation, we further introduce the \textit{MCSketch8K} dataset, comprising editable vector assets, compositional layouts, and object-level manipulation annotations. Extensive experiments show that SketchDirector outperforms state-of-the-art baselines in semantic and compositional quality while effectively preserving overall contour organization during refinement. The project page is: \href{https://yiki77.github.io/SketchDirector/}{https://yiki77.github.io/SketchDirector/}.

items.title_en: Escaping Path Mirages in Offline Goal-Conditioned Reinforcement Learning
items.title_zh: 摆脱离线目标条件强化学习中的路径幻象
items.abstract_en: Offline goal-conditioned reinforcement learning remains challenging in stochastic long-horizon settings, where compounding value estimation errors hinder reliable goal reaching. While prior methods have sought to address this challenge through various approaches, a key challenge remains path mirage, where agents overcommit to spuriously successful trajectories in offline datasets induced by stochasticity, often leading to failure on difficult tasks. To address this issue, we propose Branch-aware Graph Planning (BGP), which captures stochastic branching structures by identifying high-variability points as graph nodes and designing goal-conditioned edges with segmented learning to avoid unreliable branches and reduce unnecessary stochasticity along paths. As a result, BGP enables reliable goal reaching even in highly stochastic long-horizon environments, and experiments on diverse OGBench tasks show that it substantially outperforms prior state-of-the-art offline goal-conditioned RL methods. Our implementation is available at https://umlic.github.io/papers/BGP/.
items.comment: 10 pages (main), 34 pages in total. Accepted to NeurIPS 2026

items.title_en: Coupled Guidance for Flow Matching
items.title_zh: 用于流匹配的耦合引导
items.abstract_en: Guidance methods are essential tools for steering the generation process in diffusion models, improving the generalizability of stochastic robotic controllers and enabling high-quality controlled image synthesis. Despite strong parallels between flow-matching and diffusion, integrating guidance into flow-matching models remains quite challenging. Recent work has proposed general guidance frameworks for flow-matching, however, they are direct adaptations of diffusion guidance methods and can prove unstable. In this work, we conduct a theoretical analysis of guidance in flow-matching and show that a naive translation of diffusion-based guidance to flow-matching breaks the coupling distribution used during training, resulting in weaker control over sampling accuracy. Building on this insight, we propose Coupled Guidance, a flow-matching-specific guidance mechanism derived from a geometric perspective that leverages the coupling structure inherent to flow-matching training. To validate the effectiveness of our approach, we conduct extensive experimentation on a custom robotic collision avoidance task using ManiSkill3, four robotic dexterous manipulation tasks from the Adroit benchmark, and three image generation tasks, namely inpainting, super-resolution, and deblurring, using the ImageNet-128 and CelebA-HQ-256 datasets. Our findings show that our framework improves sample quality and guidance stability across all tasks, without imposing any additional overhead.

items.title_en: Active Constraints for Simultaneous Guidance and Safety in Handheld Micromanipulation
items.title_zh: 手持微操作中用于同步引导与安全的主动约束
items.abstract_en: In micromanipulation, erroneous hand motion limits unaided manipulation accuracy, which can affect task performance and safety in critical applications like microsurgery. Handheld robots (micromanipulators) enable motion accuracy beyond human limits by providing robotic assistance in a low-cost, compact, intuitive form factor. Particularly, active constraints are an effective form of robotic assistance, which aids the operator by restricting the robot's permissible motion based on task-specific requirements or objectives, thereby providing task guidance and enforcing safety. However, existing formulations of active constraints for handheld systems are limited, most notably because of the inability to provide guidance and enforce safety simultaneously. Implementing active constraints with optimization-based methods can address these limitations, but existing implementations are designed for free-standing robots, and neglect that handheld robots actuate relative to the operator's hand with a limited workspace. In this work, we propose an optimization-based active constraint framework for handheld micromanipulation that enables simultaneous guidance and safety enforcement. The formulation was implemented in a handheld robot and demonstrated on a medically relevant artificial task. Results show that the proposed formulation reduced safety violation rate by more than two orders of magnitude relative to baselines, while recovering the threefold accuracy loss from enforcing safety alone.

items.title_en: TACOS: Terrain-Aware COntact Supervision for Visual Footstep Planning
items.title_zh: TACOS：用于视觉脚步规划的地形感知接触监督
items.abstract_en: Humans navigate their environment based on their vision system, anticipating how the ground will respond before committing to a step. Self-supervised learning could provide legged robots the same ability, but the supervisory signal is typically chosen on intuition, and its effect on what the model learns is rarely examined. We present Terrain-Aware COntact Supervision (TACOS), which proposes a meaningful and consistent footstep instability score, based on the residual of a factor graph in legged state estimation. It projects the continuous score into preceding images to supervise a dense visual predictor. We propose two variants, a hard score that exploits hindsight and a causal soft score available immediately. Both metrics are compared against state-of-the-art alternatives in two independent evaluations that share no data or labels. On 1716 manually annotated contacts, both variants outperform every evaluated alternative at detecting instability and ranking its severity, improving pooled severity ranking by 28 % over the strongest baseline. On three outdoor test runs, our metric also trains the most accurate visual predictor, improving rank correlation by 58 % over the strongest alternative, and by a further 25 % when supplemented with onboard context. In a real-world experiment over a 50 m forest trajectory, the trained predictor handles non-geometric terrain properties such as mud and vegetation, while stepping around geometric obstacles like fallen branches. Code is available for reproducibility at https://github.com/norlab-ulaval/TACOS.

items.title_en: EgoThumb: A Vision-Driven Supernumerary Robotic Thumb for Autonomous Grasp and Holding Assistance
items.title_zh: EgoThumb：一种视觉驱动的额外机器人拇指，用于自主抓取与持握辅助
items.abstract_en: Supernumerary robotic fingers augment human dexterity by enabling a single hand to perform complex "hold-and-manipulate" tasks that typically require bimanual coordination. However, existing devices are often hindered by bulky hardware that limits interaction to large objects and rely on explicit hand motion triggers that lack environmental context. To address these challenges, we present EgoThumb, a fully open-source, vision-driven supernumerary robotic thumb. EgoThumb features a compact, dual tendon-driven finger whose actuation is relocated to the forearm, reducing distal weight while enabling precise active joint control. The system utilizes a visual imitation learning policy that maps egocentric images from a palm-facing camera directly to continuous joint positions. By implicitly decoding human intent from visual cues capturing both the hand and the object of interest, EgoThumb achieves robust autonomous manipulation and strong generalization across diverse users and environments. All hardware designs and software implementations are fully open-sourced at https://ego-thumb.github.io.
items.comment: 8 pages, 5 figures. Accepted to the IEEE/RSJ International Conference on Intelligent Robots and Systems (IROS)

items.title_en: SAGE: Semantic-Augmented Geometric Experts for Point Cloud Registration
items.title_zh: SAGE：用于点云配准的语义增强几何专家
items.abstract_en: Point cloud registration is an essential task for scene reconstruction, requiring the alignment of partially overlapping point clouds. Under low-overlap conditions, this task remains challenging because existing geometry-only methods cannot distinguish geometrically similar but semantically distinct structures (e.g., TV corners vs. desk corners and chair legs vs. table legs), resulting in incorrect correspondences. To address this geometric ambiguity, we present Semantic-Augmented Geometric Experts (SAGE), which integrates frozen pre-trained point cloud semantic representations into the registration pipeline without requiring additional sensors or fine-tuning the semantic encoder. To effectively leverage these semantic distinctions, SAGE employs a Semantic-Guided Mixture of Experts (SG-MoE) architecture. Through semantic-aware routing, SG-MoE enables each expert to specialize in distinct semantic-geometric patterns, reducing mismatches that confound geometry-only methods. With a structure-aware estimator, SAGE achieves the highest registration recall on 3DLoMatch while remaining competitive on 3DMatch. When evaluated with the same number of refinement iterations, SAGE further achieves the highest inlier ratio and registration recall on both benchmarks. These results indicate that frozen semantic representations provide effective cues for resolving geometric ambiguity in low-overlap registration.

items.title_en: SVIn+: Multi-Modal Framework for Robust Underwater State Estimation using 3D Sonar, Visual-Inertial, Water-Pressure, and DVL
items.title_zh: SVIn+：利用三维声呐、视觉惯性、水压与 DVL 的鲁棒水下状态估计多模态框架
items.abstract_en: As expansion and scalability in underwater oper- ations becomes more important and challenging, autonomous underwater vehicles (AUVs) become more relevant and the necessity for reliable autonomy more critical. A fundamental challenge in any autonomous underwater operation, from control to safe navigation and mapping, is state estimation; a notorious hard problem to address, especially in low visibility conditions. In this paper, we tackle this problem, by presenting SVIn+, a multi-sensor framework for robust state estimation of AUVs equipped with an IMU, cameras, a water-pressure sensor, a Doppler Velocity Log (DVL), and a compact 3D sonar. This framework extends an established open-source state-of-the-art visual-inertial SLAM, SVIn, by integrating water-pressure and DVL measurements into a tightly-coupled nonlinear optimiza- tion formulation resulting in improved estimates. To leverage the structural information of recently available 3D acoustic sonars while maintaining computational efficiency, we introduce a hierarchical architecture that incorporates estimates from a decoupled front-end via KISS-ICP, treated as relative pose factors within the factor graph. The proposed framework is validated through field deployments in a shipwreck and coral reef, demonstrating drift mitigation and global consistency. To support further research in underwater multi-modal fusion, the code and the datasets can be found on project website https://cmburgul.github.io/projects/svin+/ https://dartmouthrobotics.github.io/svin-plus

items.title_en: UT-HMR: Uncertainty-Guided Temporal Modeling for Robust 3D Human Mesh Recovery
items.title_zh: UT-HMR：面向鲁棒 3D 人体网格恢复的不确定性引导时序建模
items.abstract_en: Monocular 3D human mesh recovery (HMR) remains unreliable under weak observations caused by long camera-to-person distances, occlusion, and motion blur. In challenging scenarios such as sports, these factors make the problem highly ambiguous, as different 3D poses may yield similar 2D projections. This ambiguity is especially severe for one-stage HMR, which recovers all meshes directly from the full image without person crops or external 2D cues. To handle this ambiguity, we present UT-HMR ( Uncertainty-guided Temporal HMR), to our knowledge the first one-stage HMR framework to capture correlated pose uncertainty across joints. Each person query predicts a Gaussian distribution over the full SMPL pose with a compact low-rank-plus-diagonal covariance, which is converted into joint-wise precision weights for heteroscedastic supervision while keeping inference deterministic. Temporal early fusion further injects neighboring-frame evidence before pose decoding, supplying the visual evidence needed to resolve the ambiguity that the uncertainty captures. With a lightweight ViT-B backbone, UT-HMR achieves state-of-the-art results on VIP-HockeyPose-v2 (ice hockey) and WorldPose (soccer), reducing MPJPE, PA-MPJPE, and PVE by up to 4.7%, 3.8%, and 5.6%, and remains competitive on 3DPW against methods with larger backbones and higher input resolutions.

items.title_en: Closed-Loop Aware Planning via Imitation-Free Speed Scoring for End-to-End Autonomous Driving
items.title_zh: 基于无模仿速度评分的闭环感知规划用于端到端自动驾驶
items.abstract_en: End-to-end autonomous driving has predominantly relied on open-loop imitation learning for training, which presents two limitations. First, expert demonstrations show only one behavior per scenario, so the model cannot learn alternative valid behaviors and, in turn, cannot adapt to user-specified preferences at test time. Second, noise or ambiguity in these demonstrations can produce inconsistent, unreliable supervision for the end-to-end models. Driving is inherently multi-modal: multiple different behaviors can be valid responses to the same scene, and this diversity arises largely from speed rather than path. We introduce a planning paradigm that learns the path through imitation while scoring a set of candidate speeds across multiple criteria with a learned function supervised by physically grounded safety constraints. We realize this paradigm as Closed-Loop Aware Planning for Autonomous Driving (CLAP-AD), a plug-in planning head that integrates with existing end-to-end driving models and, to our knowledge, is the first to enable explicit test-time control over their speed selection without speed-conditioned training. On Bench2Drive-Speed, CLAP-AD sets a new state of the art Speed-Adherence Score of 82.53, topping TFv6, the strongest baseline on this metric, by 12.9 points while retaining strong closed-loop driving performance. On Bench2Drive, it improves driving score by +28.5 and +32.7 over UniAD and VAD, and on NAVSIM v2, built on real-world driving data, EPDMS by +6.1 over its backbone. Project page: https://clap-ad.github.io
items.comment: Accepted to WACV 2027. 17 pages (8-page main paper, references, and supplementary material), 5 figures, 7 tables. Project page: https://clap-ad.github.io. \c{opyright} 2027 IEEE. Personal use of this material is permitted. Permission from IEEE must be obtained for all other uses, in any current or future media

items.title_en: Revisiting Direct Control: A Field Evaluation of Sensor Fusion Efficacy in Teleoperating Full-Scale Autonomous Vehicles via Bird's Eye View
items.title_zh: 重新审视直接控制：通过鸟瞰图遥操作全尺寸自动驾驶车辆时传感器融合效能的现场评估
items.abstract_en: In autonomous driving, robot teleoperation serves as a critical safety fallback mechanism, requiring operators to assume direct control in the event of system failure. While recent research has pivoted toward high-level supervisory control or simulation-based studies, these approaches often fail to capture the physical dynamics and sensory demands of driving a full-scale vehicle. To address this gap, we evaluated the impact of spatial data representation on operator performance using a real car-sized vehicle in a field experiment with $N = 18$ participants. We compared three visualization interfaces: (i) a standard camera feed baseline, with two bird's-eye views (BEV) from (ii) a raw LiDAR point cloud, and (iii) a sensor fusion of LiDAR and camera data streams. Contrary to prior passive observation studies suggesting that sensor-fusion BEV may hinder awareness, our active-control results demonstrate that such representation significantly outperforms the standard LiDAR BEV in perceived usability ($p \leq 0.0001$) and cognitive task load ($p = 0.01$, NASA-TLX score: 34.58/100) while also being significantly better than the Camera-only view ($p = 0.043$). The fused interface also led to statistically significant reductions in task completion time ($p = 0.0461$) and superior usability (SUS: 77.9/100) compared to those of the Camera-only and LiDAR-only views. By synthesizing objective performance data with comprehensive subjective assessments, we demonstrate that BEV fusion maximizes safety margins while minimizing the operator's mental demand. These findings challenge existing teleoperation conventions and provide an empirically validated approach for designing robust remote piloting systems.
items.comment: Accepted at 2026 IEEE/RSJ International Conference on Intelligent Robots and Systems (IROS)

items.title_en: CSO: Refining Robotic Policies via Skill Distribution Alignment and Skill-Grained Optimization
items.title_zh: CSO：通过技能分布对齐与技能粒度优化改进机器人策略
items.abstract_en: Discretizing continuous actions into discrete skills using methods like VQ-VAE has emerged as a powerful paradigm for robotic manipulation. However, quantization errors yield a suboptimal distribution for the skill prior, degrading its performance. While reinforcement learning offers a path for refinement, its direct application faces unstable encoder updates and a granularity dilemma in importance sampling. To address these challenges, we introduce Cascaded Skills Optimization (CSO), a two-stage post-training framework. First, Rejection-Sampling Supervised Fine-tuning aligns the model's observation-to-skill mapping with the distribution of successful online trajectories via supervised fine-tuning. Second, with the observation encoder frozen, Skills Policy Optimization computes an independent, clipped importance ratio for each complete skill, enabling stable and efficient updates. With a lightweight QueST-style policy, CSO raises overall LIBERO success from 80.1% to 97.5%, improves performance on RoboTwin2.0, and achieves 61.0% success across five physical single-arm tasks. Additional comparisons with FAST, discrete BEAST, and fixed-buffer IQL further validate the effectiveness of our two-stage post-training strategy.
items.comment: Accepted at NeurIPS 2026. 31 pages, including appendices and checklist

items.title_en: Hierarchical World Models with Implicit Dynamics
items.title_zh: 具有隐式动力学的分层世界模型
items.abstract_en: Planning with world models enables test-time adaptation for embodied agents, offering superior generalization over direct policy learning. However, long-horizon tasks remain hindered by cumulative errors and search complexity. Existing hierarchical methods often use rigid macro-actions or latent skills, leading to brittle representations and limited fine-grained control. We introduce ID-WM (Implicit Dynamics World Models), a hierarchical world model that decouples state-space reachability from local control. Our framework utilizes a high-level model to sample feasible transitions across the state manifold and a low-level world model as an inverse dynamics solver to ground these transitions into precise actions. This allows the planner to identify reachable subgoals without being constrained by low-level execution details. By prioritizing local physical feasibility over global behavioral patterns, ID-WM synthesizes novel long-horizon plans from short segments, transcending the specific behavioral modes seen during training. We demonstrate its effectiveness across three navigation and manipulation suites, achieving a 38.5% improvement over state-of-the-art policy and diffusion-based planners. Crucially, by leveraging this hierarchical structure to mitigate compounding errors, our approach yields a 135% performance gain over single-level world model MPC, particularly in complex, unseen configurations for long-horizon tasks. Videos can be viewed at https://id-wm.github.io

items.title_en: SemEllipsoid: Semantic-aware Shape Abstraction with Ellipsoid
items.title_zh: SemEllipsoid：基于椭球的语义感知形状抽象
items.abstract_en: Representing 3D shapes using a set of primitives - known as shape abstraction - is an actively studied problem in computer graphics with wide applications in shape understanding, analysis, and simulation due to the compactness and computational efficiency of the primitive-based representation. Prior work has primarily focused on geometry-aware shape abstraction, where the objective is to approximate the input shape with a minimal set of primitives while preserving geometric fidelity. However, these methods often overlook semantic consistency, inevitably leading to primitives that span across multiple semantic parts. Such inconsistency can cause undesirable artifacts in downstream tasks such as part-level shape editing or manipulation. In this paper, we introduce a new task - semantic-aware shape abstraction, where the goal is to produce abstractions that are both geometrically faithful and semantically consistent, ensuring that each primitive adheres strictly to a single semantic part without crossing semantic boundaries. We propose SemEllipsoid, a novel method to address this problem using ellipsoidal primitives. The core idea is to inject semantic constraints into the primitive optimization process leveraging the availability of semantic cues from large-scale foundation models. We design a fully differentiable projection-blending-evaluation scheme to measure semantic divergence against input semantic masks, and formulate an alternating optimization strategy to iteratively solve for optimal semantic assignment and primitive configurations. Our method is non-learning-based, requiring no data collection or network training, and generalizes well to shapes from arbitrary categories. It also supports different levels of abstraction according to user demand. Extensive experiments and evaluations validate the effectiveness of our approach across several 3D shape collections.

rm.usage: 用椭球基元做紧凑的语义一致形状抽象，可作为工程机器人识别科技核心/能量单元等部件时的轻量形状表示，或为仿真中的场地/障碍物几何建模提供压缩表示；但与自瞄、导航等核心任务关联较弱。

items.title_en: Hyperbolic Inverse Reinforcement Learning
items.title_zh: 双曲逆强化学习
items.abstract_en: Inverse reinforcement learning (IRL) seeks to infer the reward function underlying observed behavior, but its predictive accuracy and interpretability depend on how that reward is computed from the underlying features. While prior IRL reward functions have been implemented through a variety of techniques including linear weights, neural networks, or other function approximators, none make assumptions about the geometry of the underlying feature space. Inspired by geometric organization observed in neural circuits, we introduce Hyperbolic inverse reinforcement learning (Hyperbolic IRL), which parameterizes reward as a function of Hyperbolic distance between the feature vector and a learned parameter vector, as well as its Euclidean distance variant. We tested our methods against a range of linear and nonlinear IRL baselines under both deterministic and stochastic policies. Our Hyperbolic approach achieved comparable performance to state-of-the-art models on established benchmarks and excelled in the low data limit and across dense environments. Applied to human navigation among multiple exhibits in a museum room, Hyperbolic IRL reveals reward structure that depends not only on individual exhibit-distance features, but also on non-separable conjunctions between them. Together, these results demonstrate that a Hyperbolic reward parameterization can improve both the predictive accuracy and interpretability of IRL, providing a framework for studying how non-separable, conjunctive structure can begin to explain behavior.

rm.usage: 从示教轨迹反推奖励函数，理论上可用于从人工操作录像中学习哨兵巡逻或战术偏好，但双曲几何假设与 RM 场景差距大，落地需大量改造。

items.title_en: Towards Understanding the Impact of Plasticity Loss on Reinforcement Learning in Stochastic Environments
items.title_zh: 理解随机环境中可塑性损失对强化学习的影响
items.abstract_en: Deep reinforcement learning (RL) is a powerful framework for sequential decision-making. Despite many high-profile successes in recent years, deep RL is known to be brittle. An emerging line of research attributes this brittleness to a loss of plasticity in neural networks. However, plasticity loss has so far been understudied in stochastic environments. We study this interplay systematically, training SAC agents on three DeepMind Control tasks augmented with controlled levels of observation and action noise. We find that plasticity-preserving methods increase learning robustness on the two harder tasks, with their advantage growing as observation noise increases, while combining resets with layer normalization underperforms resets alone at every observation noise level tested. Further, stochasticity can accelerate the loss of plasticity in harder environments, whereas in easier settings noise can act as a regularizer that sustains plasticity. Lastly, plasticity loss is most pronounced in the early stages of training. In the most challenging stochastic settings, TD instability rather than gradual plasticity loss becomes the dominant failure mode.
items.comment: 9 pages main paper, 15 pages references and appendix, 17 figures. Presented at the Nineteenth European Workshop on Reinforcement Learning (EWRL 2026)

items.title_en: ROOF: Learning Humanoid Fall Recovery under Overhead Constraints
items.title_zh: ROOF：在头顶约束下学习人形机器人跌倒恢复
items.abstract_en: A fallen humanoid beneath an overhead obstacle faces a coupled recovery problem. It must create clearance while organizing support for a stable rise, since attempting to stand before making room can further increase obstruction. We introduce a reinforcement learning method with contact-supported geometric escape guidance, which rewards incremental reduction of robot-obstacle overlap without prescribing an escape path. To achieve this, a learned motion prior, together with posture-dependent support and joint-stall costs, is proposed to shape a single policy that learns when to clear the obstacle, how to establish support, and when to complete the rise, all using proprioception alone. In simulation, it recovers in 88.5% of trials beneath plates that can only be lifted, compared with 18.9% without geometric guidance, and in 98.6% of trials beneath free plates with randomized size, mass and placement. On a Unitree G1, the deployed policy recovered in 95 of 150 attempts across seven real-world obstacle scenes, including furniture and multi-object arrangements absent from training. Project page: https://lu-yidan.github.io/ROOF/

items.title_en: Rethinking Asymmetry in Self-Supervised 3D Geometry Learning
items.title_zh: 重新思考自监督3D几何学习中的不对称性
items.abstract_en: Self-supervised learning relies on asymmetry between what a model observes and what it must explain. Recent methods learn 3D geometry from unposed images by predicting cameras and scene structure, then rendering held-out views. To avoid trivial solutions, they impose this asymmetry in the input space, restricting how views interact through separate branches or masked attention. We revisit this design with geometric accuracy, rather than rendering quality, as the main objective. When a held-out view lies between context views, the context already constrains the geometry it observes. We therefore impose the asymmetry in the 3D representation space, excluding held-out views only from the reconstructed scene while a shared backbone uses all views for correspondence. This improves depth and pose estimation over input-space designs. We further exploit view density: sparse and dense observations depict the same scene but provide different amounts of correspondence. Aligning sparse-context features with dense-context features supplies a geometric training signal alongside rendering, without a pretrained geometric teacher. We additionally align features with a frozen vision foundation model, which brings further gains. None of these signals requires geometric annotation, and the resulting model improves geometry estimation over prior self-supervised methods. Controlled experiments isolate the contribution of each component, and self-supervised pretraining also improves subsequent supervised training.

items.title_en: RAMA: Retrieval-Augmented Multi-Agent Routing with Episodic Memory for LEO Satellite Networks
items.title_zh: RAMA：面向LEO卫星网络的带情景记忆检索增强多智能体路由
items.abstract_en: Low-Earth orbit (LEO) satellite networks present a challenging routing environment due to rapidly changing topology, traffic, and link conditions. Existing deep reinforcement learning (DRL) routing methods typically rely on current observations and information encoded in network weights, limiting their ability to exploit successful past experiences. We propose RAMA, a retrieval-augmented multi-agent DRL framework with Approximate Information State (AIS), in which each satellite combines its local observation, recent routing history, neighboring state information, and retrieved entries from a per-satellite episodic memory. Retrieved experiences are integrated through a Transformer-based decision network trained with AIS-based auxiliary objectives. With weights frozen in a 140-satellite Kepler constellation, RAMA reduces mean end-to-end latency by 13.4% and 99th-percentile latency by 66.7% relative to the state-of-theart double deep Q-network (DDQN) routing method, mainly by avoiding long detours. Updated online, RAMA remains stable while DDQN degrades. On the 1,584-satellite Starlink shell 1, the reduction in mean latency grows to 93.2%, and updating RAMA online lowers its mean latency by a further 25.5%. These results demonstrate the effectiveness of retrieval-augmented memory for scalable decentralized routing in LEO satellite networks.

items.title_en: A Hybrid Path Planning Framework for Assistive Wheelchair Navigation in Dynamic Pedestrian Environments
items.title_zh: 动态行人环境中辅助轮椅导航的混合路径规划框架
items.abstract_en: Autonomous wheelchairs can improve the quality of life for individuals with mobility impairments by providing greater independence. However, reliable navigation especially in human environments is a major challenge due to factors such as dynamic obstacles, unpredictable pedestrian behavior, and the users' need to complete multiple stops along the way before reaching their final destination. This paper presents a hybrid path planning framework for multi-goal navigation in dynamic environments. The framework integrates the Traveling Salesman Problem (TSP) for global task ordering with the Potential Field (PF) method and heuristic local planners such as Rapidly-exploring Random Tree (RRT) and A-star (A*) to achieve collision-free navigation. Within this hybrid framework, TSP determines the visiting order of intermediate stations, PF transfers global path information, and local planners avoid obstacles while guiding the robot to the stations. The local planners generate feasible paths that allow the robot to follow the global trajectory and reroute to avoid static and dynamic obstacles. For this purpose, two algorithms have been developed: (i) TSP-PF-RRT and (ii) TSP-PF-A*. The performance of the proposed algorithms are evaluated using Monte Carlo simulations in crowded and extra-crowded scenarios that contain heterogeneous dynamic and static obstacles. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed hybrid framework enables efficient multi-goal navigation while maintaining safe operation in dynamic environments with humans, with TSP-PF-RRT achieving fewer or no collisions and shorter travel distances.
items.comment: 14 pages, 5 figures. Presented as a main-track paper at the International Conference of Social Robotics + ART'26, London, UK, 1-4 July 2026

items.title_en: GhostPrefix: Synchronization-Free Universal Prefix Attacks for ASR Manipulation
items.title_zh: GhostPrefix：用于ASR操控的无同步通用前缀攻击
items.abstract_en: We present GhostPrefix, the first synchronization-free universal adversarial prefix attack against automatic speech recognition (ASR) systems. Unlike prior audio attacks, which are typically crafted per utterance, require synchronization with the victim waveform, or target narrow objectives, GhostPrefix learns a short, reusable audio segment prepended to arbitrary live speech to exert real-time control over ASR outputs without knowledge of the future utterance or temporal alignment. A key challenge is maintaining stable adversarial effects across unknown, evolving speech contexts. GhostPrefix combines token-level losses with a novel representation-level objective for stable, input-agnostic effects. GhostPrefix supports three attack modes: (i) prompted prefix attacks for semantic steering, (ii) targeted prefix attacks for transcript hijacking, and (iii) untargeted prefix attacks for transcription degradation. To remain perceptually inconspicuous, we regularize prefixes toward benign environmental-sound distributions and improve robustness against over-the-air distortions. We evaluate GhostPrefix across 13 open-source ASR models from four families. In digital settings, it achieves average attack success rates of 97.6% for prompted steering and 93.4% for targeted hijacking, while driving word error rate to 1.18 under untargeted attacks. Over the air, it achieves success rates of 91.5% and 89.5% for prompted and targeted modes, respectively. These manipulations propagate into downstream AI-assisted pipelines, including voice assistants and AI note-taking tools, causing systematic semantic misinterpretations. GhostPrefix exposes synchronization-free universal prefixes as a practical, under-explored threat to real-world ASR and downstream applications. Artifacts and demos are available at https://ghostprefix.github.io/.

items.title_en: Nexus-VLA: Bridging Human and Robot Experiences via a Shared Hierarchical Semantic Latent Space
items.title_zh: Nexus-VLA：通过共享分层语义潜在空间连接人类与机器人经验
items.abstract_en: Large-scale egocentric human videos provide rich and scalable manipulation experience for robot policy learning, yet substantial embodiment gaps in visual appearance, kinematic structure, and action spaces hinder effective knowledge transfer. Existing methods often decouple cross-embodiment knowledge alignment from robot policy learning, making it difficult for human manipulation knowledge to directly and fully contribute to robot action learning. To address this issue, we propose Nexus-VLA, a hybrid policy learning framework that enables cross-embodiment knowledge transfer through end-to-end human-robot joint training, allowing human manipulation experience to directly contribute to robot policy learning. We first introduce a hierarchical cross-embodiment semantic alignment paradigm that progressively establishes shared manipulation semantics from task intent to fine-grained interactions, enabling more complete use of the manipulation knowledge contained in human videos. Building on this hierarchy, we design a shared manipulation latent representation that jointly encodes multi-level shared knowledge into an internal representation directly used for continuous action generation, improving policy learning efficiency while effectively leveraging human knowledge. Across RoboCasa-GR1, OOD settings, and real-world robot experiments, Nexus-VLA achieves an 80.5% task success rate on RoboCasa-GR1 and demonstrates strong advantages in human-data utilization, learning efficiency, and cross-scenario generalization.

items.title_en: FoAViS: Analyzing Learned Fixation Strategies in a Foveated Active Vision System
items.title_zh: FoAViS：分析中央凹主动视觉系统中学习到的注视策略
items.abstract_en: Human vision is foveated and active: resolution is highest at the fovea and falls off towards the periphery, and fixations are actively directed to locations of interest. Building a machine system that processes information in the same way lets us study gaze behavior in a controlled setting where the system's components and objectives are known. The emergence of gaze characteristics can therefore be examined systematically, which may in turn inform our understanding of biological vision. This requires a model that can sample like the fovea, handle various tasks from classification to dense prediction, and be trained concurrently with a fixation policy. In our study, we present such a system and study its capabilities and the fixation policies that emerge from it. Our system, FoAViS, samples visual input by adopting the established log-polar foveation and accumulates information in a 2D spatial memory. Due to its 2D structure, the same memory can be read out globally for classification or densely for semantic segmentation, without any architectural change. Fixations are drawn from a 2D map by a policy trained concurrently with the task. We find that learned fixation policies select more informative, task-specific locations than non-learned heuristics. These policies also shape the task representations in a beneficial way: for both classification and segmentation, models trained concurrently with a policy outperform models trained with random locations, even when the latter are provided with learned scanpaths. Moreover, these scanpaths exhibit similarities to human gaze behavior by capturing aspects of empirical scanpath characteristics. Our work marks an important step away from standard passive, single-pass architectures, towards biologically grounded models of vision. It opens a path for studying goal-directed gaze behavior and information representation in the visual system.

items.title_en: Suspended-Fabric Robotic Manipulation Surfaces: Modelling, Design Space, and Multimodular Extensio
items.title_zh: 悬垂织物机器人操作表面：建模、设计空间与多模块扩展
items.abstract_en: Robotic Manipulation Surfaces (RMS) reposition objects by deforming the surface on which they rest. A recent class of RMS suspends a continuous fabric sheet from a sparse grid of vertical linear actuators lowering the actuator density of such surfaces but how to design such surfaces so that objects can be controlled everywhere on it, and how to extend it beyond a single module so that objects can pass between modules and achieve parallel, remain open. This paper presents a separable catenary model of the suspended sheet that is fast to compute and provides both the surface shape for given actuator heights and the actuator heights for a desired local slope. The closed form inverse lets a simple PID controller position objects on the sheet, and the model relates fabric length, module span and actuator stroke to the reachable workspace, yielding a minimum fabric length bound and design charts for these surfaces. The approach is then extended to a multimodular platform in which neighbouring modules share actuators. On a $2 \times 2$ prototype, we demonstrate that centimetre-scale objects are transferred between modules and positioned within 0.03 m over a $1 m^2$ workspace with only nine actuators, enabling multi-object manipulation and opening the way to parallel manipulation.
